evidence.why: The convenience function includes the supplied plugin collection directly in a dictionary key, so a list raises TypeError before parser construction. Its cache-hit path bypasses construction and therefore plugin installation.
The factory accepts iterable plugin references, resolves them in iteration order, and passes the resulting plugins to Markdown.
Plugins are invoked sequentially during construction. Installation counts and hook order can therefore verify parser reuse and distinguish reversed specifications.

spec.question: mistune.markdown("~~removed~~", plugins=["strikethrough"]) raises TypeError, although create_markdown accepts the same plugin list. Make the convenience API accept both lists and tuples of plugin references, including names and callable plugins, while retaining parser caching. With the other arguments unchanged, lists and tuples containing the same entries in the same order must reuse one Markdown instance, without installing the plugins again. Different plugin orders must use separate instances and install plugins in the supplied order. A later mutation of a caller's list must not change an already-cached specification. Treat plugins=None as a separate cached configuration from an explicitly empty list or tuple; the two empty collection forms must share an instance. Preserve existing rendering and create_markdown behavior. Return a unified diff against production files only, without changing tests.
